newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klestil urges Austria to embrace the future.
newsitem.headline: Klestil urges Austria to embrace the future.

text.p: Austrian President Thomas Klestil told his countrymen on Saturday to shake-off their lethargy and embrace the future lest they be left behind in a fast-changing world.
Klestil's remarks came in his traditional National Day address marking the anniversary of the country's post-World War Two constitution.
"I believe the modernisation drive that we Austrians now need still lacks power and courage: courage to say goodbye to all that is outdated, to break out, to take risks," he said.
"There is too much rigidity and reticence about change that is impeding our reform efforts, in politics, in administration and among us as citizens," Klestil added.
The president, 63, recovering from pneumonia in a Vienna hospital, was too ill to deliver the speech on television, but issued a written address instead.

His unusual wake-up call came two weeks after European parliament and Vienna state elections, in which the ruling Social Democrats suffered their worst result since Austria first embraced democracy in 1918 and the far right won record gains.
Analysts said voters were protesting against the government's harsh savings package and growing disillusionment with 22 months of European Union membership.

The president appeared to be directing his address at those who voted for EU membership in a referendum, but are now concerned about cuts in welfare payments and tax rises designed to prepare the country for Europe's planned single currency.
"We are going through a dramatic change of system, for which the traditional institutions and structures have not yet found a convincing answer," Klestil said.
"We must tackle this development quickly and with commitment and the will to shape the future," he urged.
It was the first time since Klestil took office in 1992 that he failed to speak on Austria's National Day. He was admitted to hospital six weeks ago and spent several days in intensive care.
Klestil succeeded the beleaguered Kurt Waldheim and is Austria's seventh president since World War Two. His post carries no executive power.
